summative_rubric.title: Map It, Move It! — Summative Rubric
summative_rubric.purpose: Used during and after Lesson 5 (Treasure Trail Capstone) to score each child against all 5 expectations on a 4-level scale.

rows.expectation_text: sort three-dimensional objects and two-dimensional shapes according to one attribute at a time, and identify the sorting rule being used

levels.descriptor: Sorts inconsistently. Drifts attribute mid-sort. Cannot articulate a rule.
Sorts by one attribute with prompts. Names the rule with a frame.
Independently picks an attribute, sorts consistently, and names the rule clearly.
Re-sorts the same set by a different attribute and explains how the rule changes the groupings.

rows.expectation_text: construct three-dimensional objects, and identify two-dimensional shapes contained within structures and objects

levels.descriptor: Stacks blocks randomly. Cannot identify 2D shapes on faces.
Builds simple tower. Names 1-2 shapes on visible faces.
Builds a multi-block structure and names 3+ different 2D shapes inside (rotates structure to find faces).
Counts faces, edges, vertices on a 3D shape AND identifies all 2D shapes from every angle.

rows.expectation_text: construct and describe two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects that have matching halves

levels.descriptor: Cannot identify matching halves. Folds randomly without checking match.
Identifies matching halves with prompts. Sometimes finds the right fold line.
Independently identifies symmetric shapes, finds the line of symmetry by folding, and creates one matching-halves shape.
Identifies multiple lines of symmetry on shapes that have them (square = 4 lines).

rows.expectation_text: describe the relative locations of objects or people, using positional language

levels.descriptor: Uses one position word for many ('over' for everything). Cannot use the frame.
Uses 2-3 position words. Uses the frame with prompts.
Independently uses 5+ position words and the 'The ___ is ___ the ___' frame.
Combines two position words ('above and beside') and uses position vocabulary spontaneously across the day.

rows.expectation_text: give and follow directions for moving from one location to another

levels.descriptor: Gestures vaguely. Cannot give numbered directions. Cannot follow a partner's directions.
Uses words but no numbers. Follows simple 1-step directions.
Independently gives verb + number directions ('forward 3'). Follows a 3-step sequence to the target.
Plans a multi-step route in advance and writes a complete sequence.

summative_rubric.usage_notes: Score during the Lesson 5 capstone (visible from the Capstone Template). Level 3 is the grade-level expectation.
summative_rubric.layout_description: One letter page, landscape orientation, with a 5-row × 4-level grid table plus a left-most column for expectation code and text.

summative_task_script.title: Treasure Trail Capstone — Summative Administration Guide
summative_task_script.purpose: Ties the Lesson 5 Capstone Template, the 5 detective skills (Sort, Build, Match, Locate, Move), and the rubric together.
administration_steps: Before the lesson: photocopy one Capstone Template per child plus 5 extras. Print rubric. Have Junior Spatial Detective certificates ready.
Stations 1-5 (5 min each): each child rotates through SORT, BUILD, MATCH, LOCATE, MOVE.
Station 1 (SORT): sort 8 shapes. Evidence for E1.1.
Station 2 (BUILD): build with 3 blocks; find 2D shapes. Evidence for E1.2.
Station 3 (MATCH): fold 3 shapes; mark matching halves. Evidence for E1.3.
Station 4 (LOCATE): describe 3 locations on a map with position words. Evidence for E1.4.
Station 5 (MOVE): write 3-step directions; partner follows. Evidence for E1.5.
After: review the Capstone Template with each child.
summative_task_script.scoring_guidance: Use the Capstone Template as primary evidence. Level 3 is the grade-level goal.

evidence_per_expectation.E1.1: Look at Station 1 sort. Did the child pick a single attribute and sort consistently?
evidence_per_expectation.E1.2: Look at Station 2 build + shape list. Did the child find 3+ different 2D shapes?
evidence_per_expectation.E1.3: Look at Station 3 fold marks. Did the child mark valid lines of symmetry?
evidence_per_expectation.E1.4: Look at Station 4 sentences. Did the child use 3+ different position words?
evidence_per_expectation.E1.5: Look at Station 5 directions. Did the child use verb + number consistently?
